title: A meta-analytic review of experiments examining effects of extrinsic rewards on intrinsic motivation
authors: Deci, E. L.; Koestner, R.; Ryan, R. M.
inclusion_rationale: 128-study meta-analysis providing strongest evidence on overjustification. Engagement-contingent tangible rewards undermine intrinsic motivation (d = -0.40). Highest-leverage evidence for reward mechanics failure modes.

title: Does gamification improve student learning outcome? Evidence from a meta-analysis and synthesis of qualitative data in educational contexts
authors: Bai, Shurui; Hew, Khe Foon; Huang, Biyun
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q2; Q3; and Q7 with meta-analytic evidence (k=30) that shorter interventions produce larger effects. Quantifies the novelty inflation problem that was only speculated in earlier work. Complements Sailer & Homner (2020) by independently confirming that headline gamification effects are inflated by study design artifacts.

title: Gamification enhances student intrinsic motivation, perceptions of autonomy and relatedness, but minimal impact on competency: a meta-analysis and systematic review
authors: Li, Liuyufeng; Hew, Khe Foon; Du, Jiahui
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q2; and Q4 as the first meta-analysis disaggregating gamification effects by individual SDT needs. Reveals autonomy effect (g=0.638) is 2.5x larger than intrinsic motivation effect (g=0.257); while competence is hardest to move. Provides meta-analytic confirmation of the SDT mechanism proposed by Sailer et al. (2017).

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of Gamification on Physical Activity: Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials
authors: Mazeas, Alexandre; Duclos, Martine; Pereira, Bruno; Chalabaev, Aïna
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q3; Q8; and Q10 as the only RCT-restricted meta-analysis with formal publication bias testing. Active-control estimate (g=0.23) is the most defensible single number for gamification's added value; 64% effect reduction at 14-week follow-up documents temporal decay. Provides the methodological benchmark against which all other meta-analytic estimates should be calibrated.

title: The Gamification of Learning: a Meta-analysis
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q2; Q3; and Q6 as the gold-standard education gamification meta-analysis (k=40). Reveals that motivational and behavioral effects become unstable when restricted to high-rigor studies. Provides the clearest evidence of methodological inflation in gamification research; connecting to Bartos (2023) meta-analytic overestimation findings.

title: Does Gamification Work? -- A Literature Review of Empirical Studies on Gamification
authors: Hamari, Juho; Koivisto, Jonna; Sarsa, Harri
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q2; and Q7 as the first systematic review of empirical gamification research. Landmark review that established the baseline finding of context-dependent; positive-leaning-but-mixed results. Important limitation: narrative synthesis only with no quantitative effect sizes or publication bias assessment; superseded by later meta-analyses.

title: The Effects of Gamification on Computerized Cognitive Training: Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Vermeir, Julie F; White, Melanie J; Johnson, Daniel; Crombez, Geert; Van Ryckeghem, Dimitri M L
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Shows engagement gains without robust performance transfer; key for Q1 and Q10 boundary interpretation.

title: Assessing the effects of gamification in the classroom: A longitudinal study on intrinsic motivation, social comparison, satisfaction, effort, and academic performance
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q3; Q4; Q6; and Q9 as the first rigorous longitudinal study showing gamification producing worse outcomes than no gamification. Key negative-findings study demonstrating badges and leaderboards decreased motivation; satisfaction; and exam scores over 16 weeks. Provides critical counterpoint to positive-leaning reviews and connects to Diefenbach & Mussig (2019) on universal counterproductive effects.

title: A RECIPE for Meaningful Gamification
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q4; Q7; and Q10 by proposing a framework for gamification that avoids external rewards. Theoretical contribution that introduced the RECIPE framework and the critique of PBL as BLAP gamification. Directly conflicts with reward-centric approaches and anticipates the SDT-superiority finding confirmed by Sailer et al. (2017) and Li et al. (2024).

title: Undermining children's intrinsic interest with extrinsic reward
authors: Lepper, M. R.; Greene, D.; Nisbett, R. E.
inclusion_rationale: Classic experiment confirming expected rewards reduced children's free-play behavior. Foundational overjustification evidence alongside Deci 1971.

title: Effect of digital health applications with or without gamification on physical activity and cardiometabolic risk factors: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
authors: Nishi, Stephanie K.; Kavanagh, Meaghan E.; Ramboanga, Kimberly; Ayoub-Charette, Sabrina; Modol, Sébastien; Dias, Goretty M.; Kendall, Cyril W.C.; Sievenpiper, John L.; Chiavaroli, Laura
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q2; and Q8 as the largest health gamification RCT meta-analysis (k=36; N=10079). Demonstrates real-world behavior change with modest but meaningful effects (+489 steps/day). Extends Mazeas et al. (2022) with larger sample and broader health outcomes; confirming gamification's practical value in health behavior contexts.

title: Gamification for health and wellbeing: A systematic review of the literature
authors: Johnson, Daniel; Deterding, Sebastian; Kuhn, Kerri-Ann; Staneva, Aleksandra; Stoyanov, Stoyan; Hides, Leanne
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q2; and Q8 as the primary health-domain systematic review. Reveals a critical blind spot: 84% of health gamification studies used rewards but zero measured intrinsic motivation. Connects to the SDT literature by illustrating how the field's dominant behaviorist approach ignores the motivational mechanisms that determine long-term success.

title: How gamification motivates: An experimental study of the effects of specific game design elements on psychological need satisfaction
authors: Sailer, Michael; Hense, Jan Ulrich; Mayr, Sarah Katharina; Mandl, Heinz
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q2; Q5; and Q9 by mapping specific game elements to SDT need satisfaction. Key RCT (N=699) establishing that different elements serve different psychological needs; with the critical finding that autonomy could not be affected by any tested configuration. Bridges Ryan et al. (2006) theory to practical gamification design; connects to Li et al. (2024) meta-analytic confirmation.

title: An Empirical Test of the Theory of Gamified Learning: The Effect of Leaderboards on Time-on-Task and Academic Performance
authors: Landers, R. N.; Landers, A. K.
inclusion_rationale: Cleanest isolation of leaderboard mechanic: 29.61 more interactions, with time-on-task as confirmed mediator. Proof of Landers' element-mediator-outcome model.

title: From game design elements to gamefulness
authors: Deterding, Sebastian; Dixon, Dan; Khaled, Rilla; Nacke, Lennart
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1 and Q2 by providing the canonical definition and taxonomy of gamification. Foundational definitional paper that all subsequent gamification research references. Distinguishes gamification from serious games and playful design; establishes the conceptual vocabulary used across the entire field.

title: Prospect Theory: An Analysis of Decision under Risk
inclusion_rationale: Foundation for loss aversion, the mechanism behind streak mechanics. Psychological bedrock for why streaks are so powerful.

title: Do badges increase user activity? A field experiment on the effects of gamification
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q2 and Q3 as one of the longest field studies in gamification research. Two-year field experiment (N=2989) demonstrating badges significantly increased all measured activity in a real marketplace. Provides rare long-duration evidence complementing the short-term experimental work; though between-group design limits causal claims.

title: The Motivational Pull of Video Games: A Self-Determination Theory Approach
authors: Ryan, Richard M.; Rigby, C. Scott; Przybylski, Andrew
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1 and Q4 by establishing the PENS model linking SDT need satisfaction to game engagement. Foundational theory paper that provides the motivational mechanism framework underlying all subsequent SDT-based gamification research. Directly informs the theoretical basis for Sailer et al. (2017) and Li et al. (2024).

title: The Goal-Gradient Hypothesis Resurrected: Purchase Acceleration, Illusionary Goal Progress, and Customer Retention
authors: Kivetz, Ran; Urminsky, Oleg; Zheng, Yuhuang
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Foundational evidence for proximity-driven motivation (Q2; Q6); central to progress bars; milestones; and threshold design.

title: Gamification suffers from the novelty effect but benefits from the familiarization effect: Findings from a longitudinal study
authors: Rodrigues, Luiz; Pereira, Filipe D.; Toda, Armando M.; Palomino, Paula T.; Pessoa, Marcela; Carvalho, Leandro Silva Galvão; Fernandes, David; Oliveira, Elaine H. T.; Cristea, Alexandra I.; Isotani, Seiji
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q3; Q5; and Q10 by empirically documenting the exact timeline of novelty decay and familiarization recovery. First study to identify the U-shaped engagement curve (~4-week valley; ~6-10 week recovery). Connects the speculative novelty-decline findings from Koivisto & Hamari (2014) and Bai et al. (2020) to a specific temporal model with direct design implications.

title: Self-determination theory and the facilitation of intrinsic motivation, social development, and well-being
authors: Ryan, R. M.; Deci, E. L.
inclusion_rationale: Primary SDT review paper — the theoretical backbone for autonomy/competence/relatedness in gamification. Distinct from Ryan 2006 (PENS).

title: A Meta-Analysis on the Influence of Gamification in Formal Educational Settings
authors: Huang, R.; Ritzhaupt, A. D.; Sommer, M.; Zhu, J.; Stephen, A.; Valle, N.; Hampton, J.; Li, J.
inclusion_rationale: Key education meta-analysis (g ≈ 0.464). Best mechanics-by-mechanics effect decomposition available. Not in inventory despite being a major meta-analysis.

title: When Gamification Spoils Your Learning: A Qualitative Case Study of Gamification Misuse in a Language-Learning App
authors: Hadi Mogavi, Reza; Guo, Bingcan; Zhang, Yuanhao; Haq, Ehsan-Ul; Hui, Pan; Ma, Xiaojuan
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q4; Q6; and Q9 with rigorous qualitative evidence on real-world gamification misuse in self-directed adults. Documents three misuse consequences in Duolingo with competitiveness as the primary driver. Extends Diefenbach & Mussig (2019) to a population closer to NotionRPG's target users and provides specific failure-mode detail absent from quantitative studies.

title: Towards understanding the effects of individual gamification elements on intrinsic motivation and performance
authors: Mekler, Elisa D.; Brühlmann, Florian; Tuch, Alexandre N.; Opwis, Klaus
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q2; Q4; and Q7 by isolating gamification element effects on intrinsic motivation vs. performance. Key RCT showing PBL increased performance without affecting intrinsic motivation in either direction. Resolves apparent conflict between Deci et al. (1999) overjustification findings and observed gamification benefits by showing elements function as neutral incentives.

title: The Gamification User Types Hexad Scale
authors: Tondello, Gustavo F.; Wehbe, Rina R.; Diamond, Lisa; Busch, Marc; Marczewski, Andrzej; Nacke, Lennart E.
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q4; Q7; Q8; and Q9 by establishing individual differences in gamification preferences. Scale development study creating the Hexad user type framework showing different people prefer different game elements. Challenges the assumption that gamification works uniformly and connects to Buckley & Doyle's finding that conscientiousness reduces gamification benefit.

title: Demographic differences in perceived benefits from gamification
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q3 and Q7 by providing early direct evidence of gamification novelty decay. Key empirical study showing perceived enjoyment and playfulness decrease with duration of use in exercise app users. Connects to Rodrigues et al. (2022) which later quantified the exact timeline of this decay.

title: Effects of externally mediated rewards on intrinsic motivation
inclusion_rationale: Foundational overjustification experiment. Bedrock for understanding why extrinsic rewards can undermine intrinsic motivation — directly relevant to 'when gamification fails' chapter.

title: Gamification with social incentives for diabetes: 1-year RCT
authors: Patel, M. S.; Benjamin, E. J.; Volpp, K. G.; Fox, C. S.; Small, D. S.; Massaro, J. M.; Lee, J. J.; Hilbert, V.; Valentino, M.; Taylor, D. H.; et al.
inclusion_rationale: 1-year RCT showing support/competition increased steps but collaboration among strangers did not. High-quality long-duration health RCT with mechanic-level social contrast.

title: Counterproductive effects of gamification: An analysis on the example of the gamified task manager Habitica
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q4; Q7; and Q9 as the most directly relevant study to self-directed gamified task management. All 45 participants experienced counterproductive effects including gamification-caused procrastination and system gaming. Extends Hanus & Fox (2015) negative findings to the closest NotionRPG analog and reveals failure modes specific to gamified productivity tools.

title: Developing a Theory of Gamified Learning
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Introduced the element–mediator–outcome framework essential for Q1 and Q10 and resolving contradictory findings across studies.

title: Steering user behavior with badges
authors: Anderson, Ashton; Huttenlocher, Daniel; Kleinberg, Jon; Leskovec, Jure
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Large-scale badge field study demonstrating behavior steering; critical for Q2 and Q9 regarding attention shifts.

title: Negative effects of gamification in education software: Systematic mapping and practitioner perceptions
authors: Almeida, Cláuvin; Kalinowski, Marcos; Uchôa, Anderson; Feijó, Bruno
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q4; Q7; and Q9 with a comprehensive negative-effects taxonomy from 87 papers. Reveals that developers are often unaware of gamification risks. Complements Diefenbach & Mussig (2019) and Hadi Mogavi et al. (2022) by providing the systematic element-by-element failure mapping that individual studies cannot.

title: Need-supporting gamification in education: An assessment of motivational effects over time
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q3; and Q10 as the only longitudinal study of explicitly SDT-designed gamification. Demonstrates a curvilinear motivation pattern (initial decline then recovery) rather than simple decay. Directly challenges the linear novelty-decline narrative from Koivisto & Hamari (2014) and provides the strongest evidence that SDT-informed design can sustain engagement.

title: Gamifying education: what is known, what is believed and what remains uncertain: a critical review
inclusion_rationale: Best 'gap finder' for evidence quality in education gamification. Highlights that many studies are weak/inconclusive.

title: The rise of motivational information systems: A review of gamification research
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1; Q7; and Q8 as the largest-scope gamification review (819 studies). Reveals the PBL monoculture and theoretical fragmentation across the field. Updates and extends Hamari et al. (2014) and Seaborn & Fels (2015) with substantially larger coverage; confirming persistent mixed results at massive scale.

title: Measuring flow in gamification: Dispositional Flow Scale-2
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Validated flow measurement in a gamified context; foundational for Q5 and progression calibration logic.

title: Reinforcement Today
inclusion_rationale: Core for understanding variable reward schedules — operant conditioning foundations. Informs ethics of variable ratio reinforcement in gamification.

title: Gamification of Behavior Change: Mathematical Principle and Proof-of-Concept Study
authors: Lieder, Falk; Chen, Pin-Zhen; Prentice, Mike; Amo, Victoria; Tošić, Mateo
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Field experiment on self-directed habit formation; closest match to NotionRPG population for Q2 and Q3.

title: The role of trait competitiveness and leaderboard design
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Identifies trait moderators for social mechanics; important for Q6 and tailoring decisions.

title: Gamification of task performance with leaderboards: A goal setting experiment
authors: Landers, R. N.; Bauer, K. N.; Callan, R. C.
inclusion_rationale: Leaderboards induce implicit difficult goals; goal commitment moderates. Best mechanistic explanation of leaderboard effects via goal-setting theory.

title: Revealing the theoretical basis of gamification
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Meta-review mapping theory fragmentation; supports Q1 and Q10 synthesis and prevents cherry-picking.

title: Gamification in theory and action: A survey
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q1 and Q7 by surveying the theoretical landscape and identifying definitional inconsistency. Systematic survey that catalogued design and research shortcomings in early gamification work. Complements Hamari et al. (2014) but also lacks quantitative synthesis and publication bias assessment.

title: The Endowed Progress Effect: How Artificial Advancement Increases Effort
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Core experimental evidence for artificial head starts (Q2; Q9); informs milestone framing and onboarding progress mechanics.

title: On or Off Track: How (Broken) Streaks Affect Consumer Decisions
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Empirical work on streak breaks and repair mechanisms (Q2; Q5; Q9); core academic evidence for streak freeze logic.

title: Leaderboard Design Principles to Enhance Learning and Motivation in a Gamified Educational Environment: Development Study
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Design-principles paper operationalizing safer leaderboard patterns; relevant to Q6 and Q9.

title: Tailored gamification: A review of literature
authors: Klock, Ana Carolina Tomé; Gasparini, Isabela; Pimenta, Marcelo Soares; Hamari, Juho
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Systematic review of personalization approaches; informs Q3 and Q10 about whether tailoring improves durability.

title: Health Wearables, Gamification, and Healthful Activity
authors: Hydari, Muhammad Zia; Adjerid, Idris; Striegel, Aaron D.
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Addresses Q6; Q7; and Q9 by revealing heterogeneous treatment effects of leaderboards that reverse conventional wisdom. Published in Management Science (top-tier journal); demonstrates leaderboards help sedentary users (+15%) while hurting highly active users (-5%). Directly contradicts the uniform-benefit assumption and conflicts with the positive leaderboard framing in Hamari et al. (2014).

title: Defining gamification
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Reframed gamification as service enhancement creating gameful experiences; critical for Q1 and Q7 because it distinguishes superficial mechanics from value-creating design.

title: The winner takes it all – Effects of leaderboard-based feedback on cognitive performance and motivation
authors: Pickal, Amadeus J.; Stadler, Matthias; Sailer, Michael; Bai, Shurui; Ninaus, Manuel; Greiff, Samuel; Becker, Nicolas; Koch, Marco
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Experimental evidence that negative rank feedback harms intrinsic motivation; critical for Q4 and Q6 risk framing.

title: Defining, and understanding commitment to, activity streaks
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Conceptual clarification of streak commitment mechanisms (Q2; Q6; Q9); prevents conflating frequency with streak-based motivation.

title: Personalized gamification versus one-size-fits-all
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Head-to-head comparison of tailored vs generic gamification; informs Q3 and Q10 transition strategies.

title: Overcoming the novelty effect in online gamified learning systems: A longitudinal study
authors: Tsay, C. H.-H.; Kofinas, A. K.; Trivedi, S. K.; Yang, Y.
inclusion_rationale: 2-year longitudinal study showing PBL alone fails post-novelty, but PBL + meaningful pedagogy overcomes the effect. Critical for temporal dynamics chapter.

title: Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Primary theoretical source on flow and challenge-skill balance; central to Q5 progression calibration.
score_notes: Foundational flow theory. Challenge-skill balance central to game design. Seminal academic work.

title: Glued to Games: How Video Games Draw Us In and Hold Us Spellbound
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Provides the definitive SDT-based framework (PENS model) for understanding game motivation; authored by the researchers who originated the theory. Directly translates Ryan et al. (2006) empirical findings into a design-applicable framework. Essential bridge between SDT research and practical gamification need-satisfaction design for NotionRPG.
score_notes: PENS model by SDT originators. Definitive SDT-game motivation bridge.

title: For the Win: The Power of Gamification and Game Thinking in Business; Education; Government; and Social Impact (Revised Edition)
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Most accessible academic gamification framework (DMC pyramid + D6 design process) from a Wharton professor with 500K+ MOOC enrollments. Revised 2020 edition incorporates evidence from Sailer & Homner (2020) and other recent meta-analyses. Provides the structured design methodology absent from the purely theoretical research papers.
score_notes: DMC pyramid + D6 design process. 500K+ MOOC. Revised 2020 edition with updated evidence.

title: Actionable Gamification - Beyond Points, Badges, and Leaderboards
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Introduces the Octalysis Framework with its White Hat vs. Black Hat distinction that directly maps to sustainable vs. addictive gamification design. Most comprehensive practical design system with 3400+ academic citations despite being practitioner-authored. Addresses the SDT-adjacent question of which motivational drives produce long-term engagement vs. short-term compulsion.
score_notes: Octalysis framework, 3400+ academic citations, White/Black Hat distinction. Most comprehensive practitioner design system.

title: The Gamification of Learning and Instruction: Game-based Methods and Strategies for Training and Education
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Most thorough treatment connecting specific game mechanics to evidence-based learning principles. Bridges the gap between gamification research and instructional design that is missing from meta-analyses focused on outcomes. Particularly relevant for NotionRPG's difficulty calibration and feedback loop design (Q5).
score_notes: Most thorough learning + gamification bridge. Evidence-based instructional design.

title: The Art of Game Design: A Book of Lenses; Third Edition
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Provides 100+ design lenses for evaluating game experiences; especially valuable for flow-channel and interest-curve calibration. Fills the Q5 evidence gap (difficulty calibration) where academic gamification research is almost entirely theoretical. Offers practical design tools from an academic-practitioner that complement the empirical findings from flow research.
score_notes: 100+ design lenses. Flow-channel calibration. Academic-practitioner hybrid.

title: The Gamification of Learning and Instruction
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Develops the theory-of-gamified-learning model; essential synthesis text for Q1 and Q10 integration.
score_notes: Theory-of-gamified-learning synthesis. Academic text complementing Landers papers.

title: SuperBetter: A Revolutionary Approach to Getting Stronger; Happier; Braver and More Resilient
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] The only gamification book backed by its own RCTs showing clinical efficacy for resilience and mental health outcomes. Quest/power-up/ally/bad-guy framework maps directly to personal RPG design elements in NotionRPG. Provides the closest existing model for self-directed gamified personal development by a designer-researcher.
score_notes: Own RCTs showing clinical efficacy. Quest/power-up/ally framework.

title: Even Ninja Monkeys Like to Play: Gamification; Game Thinking and Motivational Design
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Created the Hexad user type framework that was subsequently validated by Tondello et al. (2016) in peer-reviewed research. Provides practical step-by-step personalization guidance for matching game elements to user types. Bridges the individual-differences research gap by offering actionable design patterns for the user-type heterogeneity documented in the literature.
score_notes: Hexad user type framework source. Validated by Tondello 2016. Personalization guidance.

title: Reality Is Broken: Why Games Make Us Better and How They Can Change the World
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Popular synthesis influencing practitioner assumptions; included for critical comparison with empirical evidence in Q7.
score_notes: Popular synthesis. Useful for critical comparison with empirical evidence.

title: A Theory of Fun for Game Design (2nd Edition)
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Central thesis that fun is the brain's reward for pattern learning explains both why novelty fades (patterns mastered) and how progressive complexity sustains engagement. Provides the theoretical grounding for the temporal dynamics documented by Rodrigues et al. (2022) and Bai et al. (2020). Essential for understanding why gamification systems must evolve to remain engaging.
score_notes: Fun = pattern learning. Explains novelty fade. Theoretical grounding.

title: Drive: The Surprising Truth About What Motivates Us
inclusion_rationale: [gamification] Widely cited SDT-inspired popularization shaping practitioner design; included to contrast rhetoric with empirical constraints in Q4 and Q10.
score_notes: SDT popularization. Widely cited but adds little beyond Ryan & Deci papers we already have.
